title: Support for latest Neptune version
body:
Hi guys, Leo here from Neptune. 

We have users requesting access to Neptune and we are currently only providing access of new requests to our latest version called Neptune Scale. I noticed in this repository that people may be using Neptune for experiment tracking and there is currently only support for the previous version of Neptune with our PyTorch Lightning integration. We understand that some users may still be using the previous version of Neptune, but raising that there are some who may be only getting access to the new version.

For this new version of Neptune, we have an [unofficial Lightning integration](https://github.com/SiddhantSadangi/pytorch-lightning) that can act as a near drop-in replacement or addition to the previous version. The major difference would be to use the `NeptuneScaleLogger` from `lightning.pytorch.loggers.neptune` for logging to Neptune Scale. The integration also supports the `NeptuneLogger` as currently implemented in the training script of this repository.

The integration can be installed from source: 
`pip install git+https://github.com/SiddhantSadangi/pytorch-lightning.git`

Packages imported, to support both Neptune versions. 
`from lightning.pytorch.loggers.neptune import NeptuneLogger, NeptuneScaleLogger`

The only nuance is to choose which version of Neptune you're using. 

Please let me know if you have any questions.

title: Filter corresponding embeddings in transform_client_ids for churn task
body:
## Description

I noticed a small issue in the `transform_client_ids` function within `training_pipeline/task_constructor.py`. Currently, for the churn task, the function filters the `client_ids` to include only those present in `active_clients.npy`. However, it doesn’t filter the corresponding `embeddings` array. Since the programs assume that both arrays have the same order, this can lead to misalignment between client_ids and embeddings.

## Proposed Change

I'd like to propose updating the function so that it accepts an additional argument, `embeddings`, and returns a tuple containing both the filtered `client_ids` and `embeddings`. This will ensure that both arrays remain aligned after filtering active clients. Note that any code calling this function will need to be updated to handle the returned tuple.

```python
def transform_client_ids(
    task: ValidTasks, client_ids: np.ndarray, embeddings: np.ndarray, data_dir: DataDir
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """
    Restrict client_ids and embeddings to active clients for churn task.
    """
    if task == ChurnTasks.CHURN:
        active_clients = np.load(data_dir.target_dir / "active_clients.npy")
        mask = np.isin(client_ids, active_clients)
        return client_ids[mask], embeddings[mask]
    return client_ids, embeddings
```

Could you review this proposal? Any feedback would be appreciated.
